sections.title: A stronger way to give a reason
sections.content: You already give reasons with mert ("because"). azért, mert is a slightly more emphatic version — azért ("for that reason") sits in the main clause, and mert introduces the reason right after it: Azért szeretek vonattal utazni, mert kényelmes ("That's why I like traveling by train, because it's comfortable" — more naturally, "I like traveling by train because it's so comfortable"). It puts a little extra weight on the reason than mert alone would.

sections.title: mert vs. azért, mert
rows: I like traveling because it's interesting.
That's why I like traveling — because it's interesting.

items.spanish: Azért imádok repülővel utazni, mert gyors.
items.english: That's why I love traveling by plane — because it's fast.

items.spanish: Azért utálok korán kelni, mert fárasztó.
items.english: That's why I hate getting up early — because it's tiring.

sections.content: azért and mert always stay paired around the same comma — most often azért opens the whole sentence (Azért szeretek utazni, mert érdekes), but you'll also hear it placed right at the end of the first clause instead (Szeretek utazni, azért, mert érdekes). Either way, mert still has to follow directly after it.
